descriptionChirho: Ramah (ha-Ramah, 'the Height'), a prominent town in the territory of Benjamin, identified with modern er-Ram about 5 miles north of Jerusalem. Principal location of Samuel's ministry (1 Sam 1:19, 7:17, 8:4, 15:34, 16:13, 19:18-23, 20:1, 25:1, 28:3), a border fortress between Israel and Judah (1 Kgs 15:17-22, 2 Chr 16:1-6), mentioned in prophetic oracles of Rachel weeping (Jer 31:15) and Isaiah's invasion route (Isa 10:29). Also listed in Joshua's allotments for Benjamin (Josh 18:25) and Naphtali (Josh 19:36). The city appears in settlement lists (Ezra 2:26, Neh 7:30, 11:33) and Hosea 5:8. Uniformly transliterated across all languages: arb ar-Ramah, kor Rama, spa Rama/Ramah. The variant 'Ramath' in Josh 19:8 likely refers to 'Ramath of the South' (Ramoth-Negev), a related but distinct southern site.
